bib.title: Complexity-Based Prompting for Multi-Step Reasoning
bib.venue: ICLR 2023 (PDF header reads 'Preprint', arXiv v2, 30 Jan 2023)

read.skipped: Appendix heading present but contains only template text ('You may include other additional sections here.'); no real appendix. References skimmed.

question: Which chain-of-thought examples make the most effective few-shot prompts for multi-step reasoning, and does the same criterion help when selecting among sampled outputs?
hypothesis: Language models' reasoning performance will increase if complex instances (more reasoning steps) are used as in-context examples, since they subsume simpler instances.
contributions: Complexity-based prompting: choose the CoT exemplars with the most reasoning steps
Complexity-based consistency: majority vote over the top K most complex of N sampled chains
New SOTA on GSM8K, MultiArith, MathQA, Date Understanding, Penguins; analysis of robustness, confounders and model scale

method.summary: Select 8 CoT exemplars with the most reasoning steps (lines split by newline) from the training set (or longest questions when no chains exist, then annotate by hand) and prompt GPT-3/Codex; at decode time sample 50 chains and vote over the top-K longest chains.
method.task: multi-step reasoning (math word problems, plus temporal, referential and commonsense reasoning)

inference.decoding: greedy (1 chain) or sampling N=50 chains then majority vote over top-K most complex
inference.samples: 50 sampled chains per question for voting; 1 for greedy; number of runs/seeds not stated
inference.prompting: 8-shot CoT (case = question + chain + answer); "Let's think step by step" added before the reasoning chains for all schemes; step = line separated by newline
inference.retrieval: Retrieval baseline: nearest training questions by Euclidean distance on Sentence-BERT embeddings (Reimers & Gurevych 2019); Centroid baseline: questions closest to the embedding centre

parameters.complexity: number of reasoning steps (newline lines); alternatives question length, formula length

limits: No variance, seeds or significance tests; single-run accuracies, dev-split (200 item) differences of 1-2 points are within noise
Gain disappears on small models (6.7B, 11B); authors call it an emergent ability of large models
Complexity helps little on Date Understanding with GPT-3 (-0.4) and StrategyQA with Codex (+0.8)
Retrieval beats complexity on MathQA (69.5 vs 42.5) because dev questions near-duplicate training questions
Mechanism for why complex prompts help simple test cases is left to future work
Tested only on GPT-3/Codex era models (text-davinci-002, code-davinci-002) and math-heavy tasks; Codex was free in Nov 2022 and code-davinci-002 is since deprecated
Optimal K tuned on dev; no rule given for choosing K
No appendix, no released prompts or code link in the text
Temperature and max tokens for sampling not stated

terms.definition: choose examples with complex reasoning chains, i.e., chains with more reasoning steps, as the prompt
sample N reasoning chains and vote only among the top K (K <= N) most complex chains; K = N recovers self-consistency
